Lone Ivy Road was reported to be flooded. The Smith River near Woolwine gage (SMWV2) rose above Minor flood stage of 9 feet by 545 AM EST and crested at 9.75 feet at 845 AM EST. This was the 5th highest stage in the period of record at this gage with data back to 1995. According to USGS data this was just below a 10-year recurrence interval flood (0.1 annual chance of occurrence).
A tree was blown down along Route 721.

The Roanoke ASOS (ROA) set date rainfall records for three consecutive days: May 19, 20 and 21 with 2.84 inches, 2.76 inches and 2.72 inches, respectively. These were also the 5th, 6th and 7th wettest days in May in the period of climate data for Roanoke back to 1912. The 3-day total of 8.32 inches ending at midnight on the 21st was easily the highest on record in May. The previous 3-day record for May was 5.70 inches in 1940. For any 3-day period it was the 5th wettest on record, trailing August 14-16, 1940 with 9.31 inches. Per NOAA Atlas 14, for a 3-day period this rainfall total is in the 90 percent confidence interval (7.27 to 8.65 inches) for a 50-year recurrence event (.02 annual exceedance probability).
A large tree limb was blown through the roof of a home. Several trees were blown down near the intersection of Route 610 and 718.
A tree was blown down by thunderstorm winds along Rich Creek Road.

Wise Avenue was closed due to overflow from Tinker Creek. This is a low-water bridge that is inundated below flood stage on the creek. The gage height on the USGS Tinker Creek above Glade Creek gage was around 7 feet at the time of this report. The stream crested at 14.77 feet on the afternoon of the 21st.

Tinker Creek was reported to be flooding portions of 13th Street from Eastgate Avenue to Mason Mill Road. The gage height on the USGS Tinker Creek Upper near Columbia gage was around 9 feet at the time of this report. The stream crested twice during the event,  at 12.58 feet late on the 20th and 13.49 on the afternoon of the 21st. Per USGS data, the peak discharge of 3920 cfs was slightly below a 5-year flood event (0.20 annual chance of occurrence) on upper Tinker Creek.

A spotter reported water several inches deep on Bennington Street from the Roanoke River around 850 PM EST on May 20th. The stage at the time of the report was around 13 feet on the Roanoke River gage at Walnut Street (RONV2). Several hour later the footbridge to the Carilion Hopsital was overrun and inaccessible. Several roads around the hospital were under varying amounts of water, up to a depth of a few feet. The reading on the Roanoke River gage was around 15.7 feet at the time of this report. The river crested at 15.89 feet at 310 PM EST on the 21st. Moderate flood stage is currently 12 feet and Major flood stage is 16 feet. This was the 8th highest stage on record at this gage, with records back to 1899. According to USGS statistics it was slightly under a 10-year event (0.1 annual chance of occurrence). Social media images also showed floodwaters from the Roanoke River covering several feet of the parking lot of the Ramada Inn and water entering the hotel, although this may have been backup along Ore Branch.

The NWS Cooperative station at Rocky Mount (RYMV2) had its wettest May day on record with 3.25 inches for the 24-hour period ending 700 AM EST on May 21st. The previous May record was 3.15 inches on May 6, 1989. A 2-day record was also established ending 700 AM on the 21st with 6.00 inches , the previous record was 4.90 inches May 11-12, 1912. At 3-days a new record of 7.80 inches was set and at 4-days the 9.25 inch total was also a record. Prior to this event, the 4-day record for May was 4.98 inches set May 20-23, 1909. A broken period of record dates back to 1894 at this site.  Per NOAA Atlas 14, for a 4-day period, the rainfall total of 9.25 inches is in the 90 percent confidence interval (8.60 to 10.1 inches) for a 50-year recurrence event (.02 annual exceedance probability).
Thunderstorm winds downed trees near Riverview.

The NWS Cooperative station at Roanoke 8 N (ROAV2) had its wettest May day on record with 3.41 inches for the 24-hour period ending 700 AM EST on May 21st. The previous May record was 2.40 inches set the day before, May 20, 2020.  Records for 3-day rainfall, at 7.99 inches and 4-day rainfall at 9.62 inches, both ending 700 AM on May 22nd were also established at this site. For a 4-day period this rainfall total is in the 90 percent confidence interval (8.81 to 10.50 inches) for a 100-year recurrence (.01 annual exceedance probability). Complete data extends only back to 1998 at this site. Among other impacts, the persistent rainfall caused the nearby Carvins Cove Reservoir to overtop the emergency spillway for only the 2nd time since 1928 and the first time since the flood of November, 1985.

The NWS Cooperative station at Woolwine 4 S (WLWV2) had its wettest May day on record with 5.52 inches for the 24-hour period ending 700 AM EST on May 21st. The previous May record was 3.61 inches on May 12, 1961. An all-time record for 3-day rainfall at 10.25 inches ending 700 AM on May 22nd was also established at this site. For a 3-day period this rainfall total is in the 90 percent confidence interval (9.57 to 11.50 inches) for a 50-year recurrence event (.02 annual exceedance probability). At a 4-day duration this station measured 11.90 inches, the 2nd highest of any 4-day period on record (after September 27-30, 2015 at 13.34 inches).  For a 4-day period this rainfall total is in the 90 percent confidence interval (11.4 to 13.7 inches) for a 100-year recurrence event (.01 annual exceedance probability). Complete data extends back to 1952 at this site. Considerable damage occurred to roads and transportation infrastructure in Patrick County according to VDOT.

The New River at Galax (GAXV2) flooded with a crest of 11.75 feet (47,600 cfs) on the afternoon of May 21st. This was the 8th highest crest on record and the highest discharge since January, 1995 (a higher stage occurred in January 2010 due to an ice jam). Stage and discharge records are available back to 1934 for this gage. According to USGS data it was roughly a 10-year flood event (0.1 annual chance of occurrence). Several roads were flooded and there was some road damage. Images on social media showed the New River well out of banks and flooding some campgrounds and equipment near Pleasant Grove Road.

The New River at Ivanhoe (IVNV2) flooded with a crest of 20.77 feet (49,800 cfs) in the late afternoon of May 21st. This was the 4th highest crest on record and the highest stage/discharge since Novermber, 1977 when the river level reached 28.08 feet. Stage and discharge records are available back to 1931 for this gage. According to USGS data it was roughly a 10-year flood event (0.1 annual chance of occurrence).

The New River at Allisonia (ALSV2) flooded with a crest of 14.16 feet (49,800 cfs) in the late afternoon of May 21st. This was the 6th highest crest on record. Moderate flood stage is 13 feet. Stage and discharge records are available back to 1930 for this gage. According to USGS data it was roughly a 10-year flood event (0.1 annual chance of occurrence).

The New River at Radford (RDFV2) flooded with a crest of 21.71 feet (93,500 cfs) near midnight on May 22nd. This was the 6th highest crest on record. Major flood stage is 20 feet and Moderate flood stage is 16 feet. Stage and discharge records are available back to 1896 for this gage. According to USGS data it was roughly a 10-year flood event (0.1 annual chance of occurrence).

The New River at Glen Lyn (GLLV2) flooded with a crest of 18.93 feet (115,000 cfs) very early on May 22nd. This was the 5th highest crest on record. Major flood stage is 18 feet and Moderate flood stage is 16 feet. Stage and discharge records are available back to 1915 for this gage. According to USGS data it was not quite a 25-year flood event (0.04 annual chance of occurrence). Lurich Road was flooded and closed according to reports.

The Dan River at Danville (DVLV2) exceeded Moderate flood stage of 26 feet, cresting at 27.57 feet early on the morning of May 23rd. This was the 3rd highest stage at the current gaging site after the remains of Hurricane Fran in September 1996 (28.65 ft.) and Hurricane Michael in October, 2018 (30.01 ft.). Flood stage categories on the Dan River were adjusted upward by several feet in May 2019. The peak discharge from this flood of 43,900 cfs was estimated to be slightly in excess of a 10-year flood event (0.10 annual exceedance probability) according to USGS studies. Several roads were closed by flooding in the Danville area.

The Dan River at Paces (PCEV2) exceeded Moderate flood stage of 29 feet, cresting at 29.13 feet on the afternoon of May 23rd. This was the 9th highest stage at this gaging site since continuous records began in 1951 and including the August 1940 flood. Flood stage categories on the Dan River were adjusted upward by several feet in May 2019. The peak discharge from this flood of 48,700 cfs was estimated to be near the 25-year flood event (0.04 annual exceedance probability) according to USGS studies. Route 658 was flooded and closed by the river.
High winds blew a tree on Old River Lane onto a power line, which fell on a house and vehicle trapping two people in the house.
High winds downed a tree one mile northwest of Hillsville on Route 52.
High winds blew down a tree on Graystone Road in Independence.
High winds knocked down a tree on Route 58 in Woodlawn.

The Dan River at South Boston (SBNV2) exceeded Moderate flood stage of 29 feet, cresting at 30.11 feet on the morning of May 24th. This was the 12th highest stage at this gaging site since records began in 1924, although there are breaks in the period of record. Flood stage categories on the Dan River were adjusted upward by several feet in May 2019. The peak discharge from this flood of 45,400 cfs was estimated to be between ad 5- and 10-year flood event (0.2 to 0.04 annual exceedance probability) according to USGS studies. Several roads around South Boston were flooded and businesses in the Riverdale area flooded.

The NWS Cooperative station at Martinsville (MARV2) had its 3rd wettest May day on record with 3.10 inches for the 24-hour period ending 700 AM EST on May 21st. The existing May record is 3.85 inches on May 19, 2018. A May record for 2-day rainfall was set with 4.95 inches ending 700 AM on May 21st and a 3-day record of 6.63 inches ending 700 AM on the 22nd. The 4-day record for May was also established at 7.73 inches. Nearly complete data extends back to 1931 at this site.

The NWS Cooperative station at Copper Hill (COHV2) had its wettest 2-day period in May with 6.03 inches ending 700 AM EST on May 22nd. The previous May 2-day record (before this event) was 4.65 inches on May 16, 1942. May records for 3-day rainfall of 7.91 inches and 4-day rainfall of 8.92 inches were also achieved ending at 700 AM on May 22nd. Per NOAA Atlas 14, for a 3-day period this rainfall total is in the 90 percent confidence interval (6.84 to 8.16 inches) for a 25-year recurrence event (.04 annual exceedance probability) and at 4-days it was in the 90 percent confidence interval (8.16 to 9.74 inches) for a 50-year event (.02 annual exceedance probability). Complete data extends back to 1940 at this site.

The Roanoke (Staunton) River at Altavista (ALTV2) reached flood stage early on the 21st and crested at 23.59 feet (31,000 cfs) early on the 22nd. This was the highest stage/discharge at this gage since September, 1996 with the remains of Hurricane Fran.

The CoCoRaHS site at Copper Hill 6.2 S (VA-FL-2) had a 4-day total of 13.66 inches of rain ending at 700 AM on May 22nd. Daily rainfall totals were 2.46, 3.22, 4.80 and 3.18 inches starting on May 19th. Per NOAA Atlas 14, for a 4-day period this rainfall total is in the 90 percent confidence interval (12.2 to 15.0 inches) for a 500-year recurrence event (.002 annual exceedance probability).

The CoCoRaHS site at Rocky Mount 2.2 NW (VA-FR-24) had a 4-day total of 11.86 inches of rain ending at 700 AM on May 22nd. Daily rainfall totals were 1.55, 3.67, 4.42, 2.22 inches starting on May 19th. Per NOAA Atlas 14, for a 4-day period this rainfall total is in the 90 percent confidence interval (10.7 to 12.9 inches) for a 200-year recurrence event (.005 annual exceedance probability).

The CoCoRaHS site at Roanoke 5.9 WSW (VA-RN-19) had a 4-day total of 11.34 inches of rain ending at 700 AM on May 22nd. Daily rainfall totals were 1.98, 2.74, 4.01, 2.61 inches starting on May 19th. Per NOAA Atlas 14, for a 4-day period this rainfall total is in the 90 percent confidence interval (10.4 to 12.6 inches) for a 500-year recurrence event (.002 annual exceedance probability). Several other CoCoRaHS sites in the Cave Spring area or Roanoke County had comparable amounts of rainfall, with amounts over 11 inches. A significant debris flow was reported near Poages Mill that covered both lanes on Sunnycrest Road and brought down a number of trees and a couple of utility poles. VDOT reported substantial damage to road infrastructure in Roanoke County.

The intersection of Craig Creek Road and Roaring Run Road was closed due to high water. The gage on Craig Creek at Parr (CRGV2) was around 13.3 feet at the time of the report. Minor flood stage is 12 feet. The stream crested at a stage of 16.20 feet (16200 cfs), the highest level since September 2004 (19.87 feet) when the remains of Hurricane Jeanne plowed through the area. It was the 7th highest on record at the gage since 1925 and was slightly below a 10-year flood event (0.1 annual chance of occurrence). Moderate flood stage is 15 feet and several roads were flooded.
Several low water bridges along Goose Creek were reported to be flooded and Goose Creek Run Road was flooded.
High winds downed trees across Alleghany county. Signs were blown down in Lowmoor.
Tinker Mill Road was flooded and Tinker Creek reported out of its banks.

Catawba Creek Road was reported to be flooded with water of unknown depth. The USGS gage on Catawba Creek near Catawba (CTWV2) crested at 7.87 feet (3660 cfs)|early on the 21st.  This was the 8th highest stage on record at this gage with data back to 1954. Only Hurricane Michael in October 2018 has had a higher stage (7.98 feet) in the past 15 years, dating back to September 2004. According to USGS data this was close to a 5-year recurrence interval flood (0.2 annual chance of occurrence).

Flooding was reported along portions of the Little River in Floyd County. Water was reported covering a portion of Thunderstruck Road due to flooding from the Little River and further downstream, Sowers Mill Dam Road was flooded. No gage is available in Floyd County, but the Little River crested a little below Minor flood stage downstream on the gage near Graysontown (GRYV2).

Walker Creek was reported to be flooding and blocking Flat Hollow Road with water several feet deep. The Walker Creek gage at Bane (BANV2) was at a stage of around 11.4 feet at the time of the report and Minor flood stage is 11 feet. The gage crested at 14.19 feet in the morning of the 21st.  Rye Hollow Road was also flooded and closed. According to USGS data the peak discharge of 13500 cfs was roughly a 5-year flood event (0.2 annual chance of occurrence).

The New River was flooding and over the top of the Dixon Ferry (Route 606) bridge on  near Fries. Social media images showed the water several feet deep with debris mixed in. Some camping equipment along the river was also flooded. The upstream gage on the New River near Galax (GAXV2) was at a stage of around 9.6 feet at the time of this report and Minor flood stage is 9 feet.

The Mill Lane low water bridge in Salem was entirely underwater and portions of W. Riverside Drive was flooded and closed along with several other roads in Salem. The nearby Salem Pump Station IFLOWS gage (SPSV2) crested at around 9.1 feet. Minor flood stage is 7 feet.

Multiple Creeks in the Buffalo Ridge area were out of their banks and numerous roadways blocked by floodwaters. The spotter reported 11.33 inches of rain in the event so far. VDOT reported considerable road and infrastructure damage in Patrick County.

The Roanoke River at Glenvar (GNVV2) crested at 14.14 feet (13400 cfs) in the early afternoon of the 21st. Flood stage is 9 feet. It was the 9th highest stage on record but data only extends back to 1992 at this gage. Several roads were closed near the river including Southwest River Road. Bohon Hollow Road bridge (Route 734) about 1 mile upstream from gage was overtopped. According to USGS statistics it was near a 5-year flood event (0.2 annual chance of occurrence).

The New River was out of its banks and blocking Big Falls Road near the Giles County line with up to 1 foot of water. Both the upstream gage on the New at Radford and downstream at Glen Lyn crested above the Major flood category.
Stroubles Creek flooded across Plantation Road.
High winds downed two trees on Route 750 and Route 600.

A vehicle was trapped in flooding from the New River along Hazel Hollow Road and a water rescue was conducted. The New River at Radford just downstream was flooding during this period and crested just above Major flood stage.
High winds brought down a tree on Route 687.
Sustained winds of 40 to 45 mph with gusts to 65 mph occurred on Five Mile Mountain just west of Calloway.
Flooding was reported over western Franklin County in the Callaway area, around Daniels Run and the South Fork of the Blackwater River.
Prillaman Switch Road was flooded in the community of Prillaman.

Several reports of flash flooding were received including a partial or complete road washouts in the Bassett area of Blackberry Road and Wells Hollow Road. Emergency Management reported several evacuations occurring or being considered. A tire facility in Bassett was badly damaged due to the flooding.

A debris flow damaged the power house at Philpott Dam knocking out power to the dam and causing some damage. According to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers which operates Philpott, the timing of the landslide is not exact but the power to the plant tripped at 6:43 PM EDT  on May 24, 2020.  The slide may have started slowly a little before that time but the mass damaging slide would have been around the time of power failure. The slide occurred in the utility right of way cleared land area that goes up from the powerhouse transformer and switch yard up the hill on the AEP grid system on the Henry County side of the Dam.
A mudslide was reported on Fairystone Park Highway near Trent Hill Drive.

Several more roads were reported to be washed out including Sleeping Hill Farm Road and Machinery Drive. A roadway was flooded at the intersection of West Fayette Street and Appalachian Drive, possibly by flooding from the Smith River and flooding tore down a tree.
Carson Drive in Bassett was blocked by a mudslide.

The Smith River was reported to be completely flooding over River Road in Fieldale near Shadyview Road. The Smith River at Bassett (BASV2) stage was around 12 feet near the time of this report. The river crested at 13.35 feet (14400 cfs) around 822 EST per USGS statistics. No flood stage had been set at this gage mainly due to the flood control exercised by Philpott Dam. But the stage was the 2nd highest since dam began operation in 1952, after the flood in September, 1987 of 15.20 feet. It should be noted that Philpott Dam lost power earlier in the evening due to a mudslide and the dam operators were unable to reduce downstream flows to the normal extent.
The bridge over Stuart Creek on Meeks Road in southern Henry County was washed out.
Blackberry Creek flooded a home along Blackberry Road near Mary Hunter Drive and Foley Drive.
A water rescue was performed along a portion of Cox Road in the Ridgeway area.

The Smith River at Martinsville (SMWV2) gage exceeded its Minor flood stage of 11 feet and crested at 12.87 feet early on the 25th. There were several reports of the Smith River flooding roadways and the river was reported to be overtopping the bridge at Daniels Creek Road. This was the 7th highest stage on record at this gage since the completion of Philpott Dam in 1952 and the highest since January 2010 (15.19 feet). Records date back to 1929 at this site but pre-1952 stages were not affected by the presence of Philpott Dam.
The West Jefferson AWOS measured sustained winds of 45 mph and a wind gust to 62 mph.
A 58 MPH wind gust was measured.
Two trees were blown down across Redstone Road In Chilhowie.
Thunderstorm winds gusted to 62.5 mph and downed a cedar tree and a bradford pear tree near the airport in Danville.

The COOP station at Bedford 4 NW (BDFV2) had 5.67 inches of rain in the 4-day period ending 700 AM EST on the 22nd. This was the 4th highest 4-day total for the month of May with broken records back to 1893. The existing 4-day records are all from the month of May 2018.
News reports showed Toms Creek flowing across the Route 654 (Brooksfield Road) one-lane bridge and flooding all the nearby lowlands. The road was closed.

The Craig Creek at Abbott (ABBV2) IFLOWS gage crested at 10.6 feet around midday on May 21st. This was the 3rd highest crest in the fairly short (since around 2010) and erratic history at this gage site. Some roads were flooded and partially damaged Craig County according to VDOT information.

The COOP station at New Castle (NWCV2) had a 2-day rainfall total of 4.77 inches ending at 700 AM EST on the 22nd which was a record for the month of May and 9th highest for any 2-day period. For the 3-day period ending the same day, the station recorded 6.12 inches, the highest ever for May and 4th highest for any 3-day period. The 3-day total was in 90 confidence interval (5.65-6.63 inches) for a 25-year rainfall event (.04 annual chance of occurrence). Extensive road damage was reported by VDOT in the County.

The New River at Glen Lyn (GLLV2) crested at 18.24 feet, just above the Major flood stage of 18 feet very early in the morning of May 22nd. This was the highest stage since the remains of Hurricane Michael in October 2018 and the 5th highest on record since 1940. The peak discharge of 115,000 cfs was somewhat less than a 25-year recurrence interval (0.04 annual chance flood) according to USGS data. Several roads near the river were flooded and closed.
A couple large trees were uprooted on a private lot.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a tree and a power line, blocking passage on Sunnybrook Circle.
A tree was blown down by thunderstorm winds across Carver Road.
A tree and a couple power lines blown down by thunderstorm winds onto Providence Lane.
A tree was blown down across Joseph Martin Highway.
A few trees were blown down by thunderstorm winds around the City of Martinsville.
One tree was blown down by thunderstorm winds across Lee Ford Camp Road.
A couple trees down were blown down by thunderstorm winds around the Ridgeway area.

Consistent rainfall over several days saturated the ground, allowing for a strong wind to knock down a tree onto a mobile home, causing significant damage to the structure and killing one occupant who was in his bedroom.

The South Fork of the New River was reported to be flooding over the bridge on Kings Creek Road near the intersection with Garvey Bridge Road. The roadway was impassable due to deep flowing water.  The river gage on South Fork of the New River near Jefferson (JFRN7) was near 8.92 feet at the time of the report which was right at the crest. Minor flood stage is 8 feet. Several other roads near the river were also flooded including part of Farmers Fish Camp Road with several feet of water.

The COOP station at Boone 1 SE (BOON7) had 8.51 inches of rain in the 4-day period ending 700 AM EST on the 22nd. This was the highest 4-day total for the month of May with records back to 1981. The old record was 7.19 inches ending on May 8, 2013. Even if the previous Boone COOP site is considered, with data back to 1929, it was still the wettest 4-day period in May on record. A record was also set at 3-days (7.51 inches) and 2-days (6.51 inches) ending at 700 AM on the 21st.

The Watauga River flooded with the USGS gage at Sugar Grove (SGWN7) reaching a stage of 8.85 feet early on the 21st. Minor flood stage is 6 feet. Several low water bridges were closed and roads along the river affected.

The COOP station at Transou (LSPN7) had 8.62 inches of rain in the 4-day period ending 700 AM EST on the 22nd. This was the highest 4-day total for the month of May with records back to 1946. The old record was 7.57 inches ending on May 19, 2018. A record was also set at 3-days (8.07 inches) and 2-days (7.28 inches) ending at 700 AM on the 21st.

The persistent heavy rains produced a substantial landslide in Salem in the 2400 block of Franklin Street. An eyewitness in a media report described it, 'all of a sudden the land just started moving. The whole point of the mountain started sliding down, trees falling everywhere.'  A nearby CoCoRaHS site in Salem (VA-RN-21) measured 10.70 inches in the 4-day period ending 700 AM on May 22.

Local news reports said many roads were flooded and damaged across Franklin County. Several were closed due to large mudslides, including Five Mile Mountain Road in southern Franklin near the Floyd County line. A section of Virginia 116 (Jubal Early Highway) in the Coopers Cove area was as the road collapsed in the early morning hours on May 22 during prolonged rainfall, according to VDOT officials. VDOT estimated that repairs would take approximately one to two months before the road can reopen to traffic. Dozens of other roads were closed at various times due to flooding.
The COOP site at Pearisburg 4 SSE (STFV2) measured 4.15 inches in the 3-day period ending at 700 AM on May 22nd. This was the 2nd highest 3-day total in May with records back to 1952.

Several news outlets reported the closure of heavily traveled Route 460 due to road damage and a large mudslide.  The mudslide occurred about five miles east of the West Virginia line. VDOT provided road repair estimates.
Media reports showed water overtopping a portion of Spring Valley Dam in Roanoke leading to the evacuation of 13 homes due to the potential risk of a dam failure.

The COOP station at Keysville 2 S (KYSV2) measured 4.17 inches of rain in the 24-hour period ending 700 AM EDT which was the highest 1-day total  on record for any June day. The previous June record was 3.75 inches June 2, 1997. It was also the 6th highest for a calendar day. Precipitation data at this site dates back to 1979 with some breaks.

The COOP station at South Boston (SOBV2) had a 24-hour rain total of 5.55 inches ending at 700 AM on the 18th, the 2nd highest on record in the month of June, after the 6.98 inches on June 23rd, 1995. It was also the 4th highest for any calendar day. The station also had a 2-day rain total of 8.80 on and a 3-day total of 10.54 inches ending 700 AM on the 18th. This was the highest 2-day total for June. beating June 24, 1995 with 8.02 inches. It was also 2nd highest amount for any calendar 2-day period. The still-existing 2-day record is 8.83 inches September 6-7, 1996 during the passage of remains from Hurricane Fran. Data extends back to 1981 at this site. The 2-day, 8.80 inch amount is in the 90 percent confidence interval (7.90-9.57 inches) for a 100-year rain event (.01 annual chance of occurrence) per NOAA Atlas 14. The 3-day total was also a new record for the site, exceeding the 9.87 inches that also occurred during Fran in September, 1996. The 3-day, 10.54 inch amount is in the 90 percent confidence interval (9.29-11.4 inches) for a 200-year event (.005 annual chance of occurrence) per NOAA Atlas 14. Data extends back to 1981 at this station.
Emergency Management reported Route 219 was flooded and several cars were in danger of washing off the road. Water was also entering a nearby house.
Country Club Road was closed due to flooding near Prospect Road.
Roark Mill Road near Melody Springs Road and Starkey Road near Glade Road were closed due to high water.
Ricky Van Shelton Drive was closed due to high water.

The NWS Cooperative station at Rocky Mount, VA (RYMV2) set a date rainfall record for June 18th of 2.65 inches for the 24-hour period ending 700 AM EDT on the 18th. The previous date record was 1.63 inches set in 1940. Nearly unbroken precipitation records exist at this station back to 1894, one of the longest running sites in the WFO Blacksburg area of responsibility.

The NWS Cooperative station at Copper Hill (COHV2) had its 2nd wettest June day on record, and 4th wettest of any calendar day, as 6.65 inches of rain fell in the 24-hours ending 700 AM EDT on the  18th. The existing June (and all-time) record is 8.21 inches on June 21, 1972 during the remnants of Hurricane Agnes. Per NOAA Atlas 14, for a 24-hour period, this rainfall total is in the 90 percent confidence interval (6.37 to 7.72 inches) for a 50-year recurrence (.02 annual exceedance probability). Complete data extends back to 1940 at this site.

Walnut Avenue near Glade Creek was closed due to water flowing over it. Flooding also occurred along Tinker Creek where the USGS gage near the confluence of Glade Creek crested at 16.96 feet in the afternoon of the 17th. No flood stage has been set at this relatively new gaging station, but Tinker Creek overflows the low-water bridge on Wise Avenue at a stage of around 7 feet.

The NWS Cooperative station at Pulaski 2 E (PSKV2) set a daily rainfall record for June 18th with 2.90 inches for the 24-hour period ending 700 AM EST on the 18th. The previous date record was 1.57 inches in 1972. It was also the 4th highest rainfall for any June day, well behind the record of 3.54 inches on June 28, 1976. This site has nearly complete rainfall data since 1940.

The IFLOWS stream gage at Pulaski (PCRV2) rose rapidly in response to heavy rainfall during the later afternoon and evening of June 17th, cresting at 9.5 feet. Flood stage is 8 feet. Several roads were flooded in the Pulaski area along Peak Creek and Tract Fork. It was the 3rd highest stage in the erratic 10-year record at this gage site.
A social media post showed the road completely flooded in front of the Cloverdale Post Office.
Flood waters were reported to have reached some mobile homes in the Wildwood Mobile Home Park. Some evacuations were conducted in the area.

The NWS Cooperative station at Covington, VA (CFPV2) set a date rainfall record for June 18th of 2.70 inches for the 24-hour period ending 700 AM EDT on the 18th. The previous date record was 1.49 inches set in 1973. It was also the 5th wettest June day on record, but well behind the record 4.20 inches on June 24, 2016. Nearly unbroken precipitation records exist at this station back to 1961 at this site.

The NWS Cooperative station at Altavista, VA (ALTV2) set a date rainfall record for June 18th of 2.62 inches for the 24-hour period ending 700 AM EDT on the 18th. The previous date record was 0.73 inches set in 2015. Precipitation records exist at this station back to 1945.
Bonsack Road and Glade Creek Road were closed due to flooding, most likely from nearby Glade Creek.
A portion of 13th Street in Roanoke was closed due to urban flooding with water flowing over the road.
Numerous roads were flooded and closed in Covington including South Craig Avenue, South Royal Avenue and and South Highland Avenue.
Up to a foot of water was observed flowing over Valley Ridge Road at the corner of Woodland Road and Magnolia Street.
Berry Hill Road was flooded and closed, most likely from Poplar Creek.
There were numerous reports of flooded roads across Halifax County, mainly in the South Boston area.

There were several reports of flooded roads in the Springville area as well as a rescue from a vehicle and from a home. Water was also reported over Wrights Valley Road and St. Clairs Crossing from flooding of nearby Wrights Valley Creek. Lynn Hollow Road was also flooded with volunteer fire officials on scene. In addition, several mudslides occurred along Route 460 between Springville and Bluefield, with traffic stopped by VDOT for a time.
A weather observer in Springville measured 2.40 inches of rain between 345 PM and 500 PM local time.
Water was flowing over several roadways in the Wirtz area and spilling out of a dentention pond near the Post Office. The Postal employee described the water as like a river.

Water over six inches in depth was seen flowing over portions of Highway 159 after 1.5 inches of rain fell in a short duration. The water was not from Dunlap Creek itself which had returned to below flood stage from the previous day.
The USGS gage on Dunlap Creek (DLPV2) rose briefly above minor flood stage of 9 feet early on the 18th, cresting at 9.16 feet. Several roads very close to the creek may have been flooded.
Miller Creeks Road was reported to be washed out by flash flooding.
Ferry Street was closed near Seymour Drive due to water flowing over the road, possibly from Poplar Creek.
Flooding at the intersection of Rocky Ford Road and Culpeper Lane closed the road.

Wilkerson Mill Road was closed near Route 460, most likely from nearby Goose Creek. The USGS gage on Goose Creek near Huddleston (HUDV2) rose over minor flood stage of 15 feet around midday on the 17th and crested at 16.87 feet by 215 PM EST. It was the highest stage in over 10 years at this gage, going back to January 25, 2010 when it reached 18.66 feet.
Water of unknown depth was reported over Chalk Level Road.
The road and culvert were washed out at the corner of Summit Ridge Drive and Brentwood Drive.

The COOP observer at Bedford, VA (BDFV2) had its second highest date rainfall for the 24-hours ending 700 AM on June 17th with 2.49 inches, behind the 1934 record of 2.77 inches. The following 24-hour period ending at 700 AM on the 18th, again saw a second highest amount for the date with 2.39 inches, after the 1936 record of 2.80 inches. The 2-day total of 4.88 inches was the second highest on record in the month of June, after the 5.36 inches on June 23-24, 1995. Precipitation data at this site date back to 1893 but with significant gaps in the record.
An unofficial 24-hour rainfall amount of 7.86 inches was reported near South Boston ending around 100 PM local time on the 17th. There were numerous flood reports from the area.

An automated site on the east side of South Boston measured 7.42 inches on June 17th (ending at midnight on the 18th). Although an unofficial site, this amount equates to the 90 percent confidence interval (6.97-8.47 inches) for a 100-year rainfall event (.01 annual exceedance probability).
Several roads were closed across Montgomery County including Meadow Creek ROad, Goldrush Road and others on the VDOT VA 511 website.

The USGS gage on Johns Creek at New Castle (JCRV2) crested at 11.03 feet on the afternoon of June 17th after heavy rains the previous two days. This was the highest stage reached at this site since September 28, 2004 when it reached 12.87 feet and the 6th highest since records began in 1927. The 3-day rainfall at the nearby NWS COOP site at New Castle was 4.12 inches.

The gage on Craig Creek at Parr (CRGV2) crested at a stage of 14.24 feet (12500 cfs) very early on June 18th. It was the 8th highest on record at this gaging station since 1925 and was approximately a 5-year flood event (0.2 annual chance of occurrence) according to USGS studies. A road or two was likely affected.

The USGS stream gage on Walker Creek at Bane (BANV2) crested at 13.55 feet early on the 18th. Several roads were closed near the creek. The nearby COOP site at Pearisburg 4 SEE measured 5.04 inches of rain in the 4-day period ending 700 AM on the 18th.

The USGS gage on Indian Creek at Red Sulphur Springs (INCW2) rose above minor flood stage of 10 feet in the afternoon of the 17th cresting at 11.18 feet. Several roads were flooded and a report of flooding along a portion of Indian Creek Road was received.
Buggy Branch was well out of its banks and flooding the Pence Springs Flea market off Route 12/3.

Reports mentioned up to 25 homes damaged on the Monroe County side of Alderson. Two homes suffered severe structural damage when basement walls were caved. Dark Hollow Road was flooded out and the bridge possibly damaged. At least one person was reported trapped in their home and requiring rescue. Follow-up reports mentioned several mudslide and some very significant road and culvert damage in parts of the area.

Severe flash flooding closed Route 12 and Route 63 into Alderson. Up to 12 homes received flood damage on the Greenbrier side of Alderson and several road culverts were destroyed.  A photo from broadcast media showed Muddy Creek Mountain Road washed out.

The COOP observer at Alderson measured 2.50 inches for the 24-hour period ending 700 AM on the 20th. This was a daily record for the date, beating the previous record of 1.45 inches in 1987. It was also the 6th highest daily rainfall in June with nearly complete data back to 1944. Nearby automated rain gages indicated that most of the rain fell in about a 90-minute period between about 430 and 600 PM local time, although news reports suggested a 45-minute time frame for the rainfall.

The CoCoRaHS station at Alderson 0.8 SSW (WV-MR-2) recorded 2.24 inches for the 24-hour period ending at 700 AM on the 20th, but most of the rain fell in roughly 50 minutes on the afternoon of of the 19th. Significant flash flooding was reported in the area.

A home mesonet station recorded a storm total 4.67 inches of rain.  Most of this fell in a 2-3 hour period, which equated to roughly a 150-year rainfall event during the 2 and 3 hour time periods per NOAA Atlas-14 point analysis.

A CoCoRaHS observer recorded a storm-total rainfall amount of 4.12 inches, much of which fell during at 2 to 3 hour time period.  This equated to an estimated 150-year event for this location per NOAA Atlas-14 point analysis.

Thunderstorms produced 3 to 4 inch rainfall amounts, with locally higher amounts in spots, across the town of Yadkinville and central portions of Yadkin County.  Most of this rain fell within a 3-hour timeframe.  Runoff from this rain caused numerous roads in the area to be flooded and impassible until the flood waters receded.  Among the roads that were flooded were Billy Reynolds Road and Booger Swamp Road in Yadkinville.

A home mesonet station recorded a storm total 3.96 inches of rain. Most of this fell in a little over 2 hours, which equated to a little over a 100-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas-14 point analysis.

A CoCoRaHS observer recorded at storm total amount of 3.78 inches of rainfall.  The observer noted that 2.1 inches fell in about 45 minutes, estimated to be around a 50-year rainfall events for this duration.

The Cooperative Weather Observer in North Wilkesboro, NC recorded 1.94 inches of rain from thunderstorms over the area.  Much of this rain fell between over a 2-hour period during the afternoon.
