Emergency Services personnel in the community of Mt. Airy reported that portions of both North Franklin and South Franklin Streets were under several inches of standing water as storm sewers were overwhelmed by prolonged periods of heavy rainfall.  Portions of both roads were impassible until the water receded.  No damage or injuries were reported.

Seed Cane Creek flooded out of its banks across Reeves Mill Road, making the road impassible.  Two separate swift water rescues took place when two automobiles were caught in the flooding and the occupants were rescued.  No injuries were reported.  Some water damage occurred to each vehicle.

Multiple roads between the communities of Mt. Airy and Ararat were flooded and impassible by as much as a foot of flowing water over the roadways in spots.  This was caused by heavy rainfall of 3 to locally 5 inches within a 3-hour period that caused several streams and creeks to overflow their banks across the roadway surface.  Roads that were reported impassible by flood waters included, but were not limited to, Hiatt Road at Stoney Creek, Quaker Road at Faulkner Creek, Armstrong Road by Flat Shoal Creek, Westfield Road along Rutledge Creek and Reeves Mill Road along Seed Cane Creek.  No damage to the roads themselves were reported, however some debris removal was necessary to make the roads passable again.

Heavy rain of up to 2.25 inches in 2 hours caused Stoney Creek to rise rapidly for the 2nd time in 24 hours.  Flooding from Stoney Creek forced residents of a home on Christy Lane to evacuate.  Hiatt Road was also impassible due to flood waters from Stoney Creek passing across the road.  The road reopened after flooding receded.  No damage or injuries were reported.

Runoff from heavy rain was observed overflowing a small creek at the along Phelgar Street and running 6-8 inches deep across the road near the intersection with 2nd Street.  One block downstream, along 1st Street, water was overflowing the banks of the same creek, and was entering Cook's Clean Center.  Water entered the building several inches deep.

Town Branch, a tributary of Crab Creek, was observed overflowing its banks near the intersection of Depot Street and Stone Street, and was flowing several inches deep across the road surface.  The road reopened after flooding subsided, with no damage observed.

Heavy rain, falling at prolonged rates of 2 to 3 inches per hour, caused Dry Creek to flood out of its banks several inches deep across Beale Trail Road.  No damage to the road was observed and the road was passable again after flooding receded.

Heavy rain, falling at prolonged rates of 2 to 3 inches per hour, caused a tributary of Goose Creek to flood out of its banks several inches deep across Crouch Road. The flooding caused the culvert running beneath the road to fail, making the road impassible until the damage was repaired and the culvert replaced.

Heavy rain, falling at prolonged rates of 2 to 3 inches per hour, resulted in several inches of standing water across Highway 460, making the road impassible until the flood waters receded.  No damage was reported during this event.

Severe Drought conditions were declared for the southern half of Charlotte County on November 30th after a month of extremely low rainfall totals. The CoCoRaHS observer at Saxe 4.3 SE (VA-CH-1) measured only 0.10 inches of precipitation for the month, less than 3 percent of the normal amount. No burn bans were put into effect during the month however. NASA SPoRT LIS data estimated that average soil moisture in the top 100cm soil was between the 10th and 5th percentiles, an indicator of severe dryness, and county streamflows below-normal per the USGS WaterWatch website. There were no reported impacts to agriculture and livestock given the late time of the year. There were no wildland fires were reported burning within the county.

Severe Drought conditions were declared for the extreme southeastern portion of Pittsylvania County on November 30th after a month of extremely low rainfall totals. The ASOS At Danville Regional Airport (DAN) measured only 0.15 inches of precipitation for the month, or only about 4 percent of the normal amount of 3.46 inches.  This makes November 2021 both the driest November and the 4th-driest month on record dating as far back as 1916.  Because of the dry conditions, officials for both the City of Danville and Pittsylvania County issued a burn ban effective 6:00 pm on the 30th preventing any type of outdoor burning. NASA SPoRT LIS data estimated that average soil moisture in the top 100cm soil was around the second percentile, an indicator of extreme dryness, and county streamflows ranged from below-normal to well below-normal per the USGS WaterWatch website.  However, impacts to agriculture and livestock were limited given the late time of the year.  No wildland fires were reported burning that day within the county or the City of Danville.
Flyblow Creek flooded a portion of Route 618/Farmers Road, one mile west of Renan.

Severe Drought conditions were declared for the southern half of Halifax County on November 30th after a month of extremely low rainfall totals. The Cooperative Weather Observer (COOP) at South Boston (SOBV2) measured only 0.33 inches of precipitation for the month, nearly 10 percent of the normal amount of 3.40 inches. This month was the 2nd driest November on record for this COOP dating back to 1971, and the 4th driest month overall. No burn bans were put into effect in the county during the month. NASA SPoRT LIS data estimated that average soil moisture in the top 100cm soil ranged between the 10th and 2nd percentiles, an indicator of severe to locally extreme dryness, and county streamflows varied between below-normal and well below-normal per the USGS WaterWatch website. There were no reported impacts to agriculture and livestock given the late time of the year. There were no wildland fires were reported burning within the county.

This month was the driest November on record for this COOP dating back to 1996, and the 2nd driest month overall. Caswell County was included in a state-wide burn ban for North Carolina that was implemented on November 29th. NASA SPoRT LIS data estimated that average soil moisture in the top 100cm soil ranged between the 10th and 2nd percentiles, an indicator of severe to locally extreme dryness, and county streamflows varied between below-normal and well below-normal per the USGS WaterWatch website. There were no reported impacts to agriculture and livestock given the late time of the year. There were no wildland fires were reported burning within the county at month's end.

Severe Drought conditions declared for the southern half of Charlotte County at the end of November persisted through December after another month of precipitation that was significantly below normal. The CoCoRaHS observer at Saxe 4.3 SE (VA-CH-1) measured 1.17 inches of precipitation for the month, about 30 percent of the normal amount. NASA SPoRT LIS data estimated that average soil moisture in the top 100 cm soil at the start of the month was between the 10th and 5th percentiles, an indicator of severe dryness, and only decreased below the 2nd percentile by the end of the month. County streamflows remained below normal through the month per the USGS WaterWatch website. There were no reported impacts to agriculture and livestock given the late time of the year. A burn ban was put into effect for the county on December 2nd, and lifted December 20th after a widespread rainfall event. There were no wildland fires reported within the county.

Severe Drought conditions declared for the extreme southeastern portion of Pittsylvania County at the end of November persisted through December after another month of precipitation that was significantly below normal. The ASOS at the Danville Regional Airport (DAN) measured only 0.65 inches of precipitation for the month, or only about 21 percent of the normal amount of 3.06 inches. NASA SPoRT LIS data estimated that average soil moisture in the top 100 cm soil at the start of the month was between the 10th and 5th percentiles, an indicator of severe dryness, and only decreased below the 2nd percentile by the end of the month. Local streamflows, including the Dan River at Danville (DVLV2), remained below normal through the month per the USGS WaterWatch website. There were few impacts to agriculture and livestock given the late time of the year, affecting cover crops designed to reduce soil erosion with only miniscule growth. It is not known if this resulted in a financial impact as cover crops are not harvested. A burn ban, implemented in late November, remained in effect for the county and the City of Danville for the entire month, however there were no wildland fires reported.

NASA SPoRT LIS data estimated that average soil moisture in the top 100 cm soil at the start of the month was between the 10th and 5th percentiles, an indicator of severe dryness, and only decreased below the 2nd percentile by the end of the month. As of December 4th, 2021, the cost of containing the Grindstone Fire on Pilot Mountain has increased to at least $364,000 dollars and has burned an estimated 1050 acres of state park land.  The fire is now 100% contained.  The fire was caused by a campfire that escaped containment during unusually dry conditions and high winds favorable for allowing the fire to quickly spread.

The Clinch River in Richlands crested at 10.33 feet at 8:00 am on the 2nd, just above the minor flood stage of 10 feet.  Imagery taken by a drone indicated generally minor impacts due to the flooding.  Most noteable of these impacts was flooding along 4th Street near the Richlands Police Department, where backwater flooding of nearby Big Creek caused multiple homes to be surrounded by flood waters.  Though water did not enter the living space of these homes, they were evacuated out of precaution.  At least two cars parked along 4th Street were submerged up to the tops of their tires, with water entering the passenger cabins.

An automated weather station (Weather Underground: KVAJEWEL2) in the northern part of the Clinch River Basin observed a 10-hour rainfall total, ending 6 AM EST on the 2nd, of 2.88 inches.  This amount is estimated to be between a 5- and 10-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas 14 point frequency estimates for this duration.
The Cooperative Weather Observer at Richlands, VA (RCLV2) observed a 24-hour precipitation total ending 12Z (7:00 AM EST) of 1.84 inches, a new station record total for that date.
